instruction: Extract and load the Chrome extension from /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip. Make sure the extension icon file is present.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: This task verifies that the extension icon file (hello_extensions.png) exists in the extracted extension directory. Verified from zip file listing.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete instruction coverage: instruction requires 'Extract AND load the Chrome extension' but evaluator only verifies file extraction, not extension loading in Chrome

Critical semantic gap: evaluator checks if icon file exists in filesystem (/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension/hello_extensions.png) but does not verify the extension was actually loaded/installed in Chrome browser
Evaluator would pass even if user never loads the extension into Chrome, as config already extracts the zip file automatically
Missing Chrome extension state verification: should check chrome://extensions/ or use Chrome DevTools Protocol to verify extension is installed and enabled
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add getter to check Chrome extension state via CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol): query installed extensions list and verify helloExtension is present and enabled
Alternative: use accessibility tree or screenshot analysis to verify extension icon appears in Chrome toolbar or extensions page
Consider splitting into two separate tasks: (1) Extract extension files (current evaluator), (2) Load extension in Chrome (new evaluator with Chrome state verification)
If keeping as single task, add postconfig to navigate to chrome://extensions/ and verify extension appears in the list
